ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (Public Act No. 35 of 2009); Companies Act 1993 (Public Act No. 105 of 1993); Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; Sanctions Act 2019; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Regulations 2009. New Zealand does not operate a public UBO register; beneficial-ownership information is obtained under the AML/CFT customer due diligence regime and retained in private AML/CFT compliance files accessible to the Department of Internal Affairs, Financial Markets Authority, and Reserve Bank of New Zealand.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of biometric page of passport of each ultimate beneficial owner and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or authorized Commissioner for Oaths in the UBO's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original or certified utility bill or bank statement evidencing residential address of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or bank in the UBO's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incumbency for each corporate shareholder holding 25% or more
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or registered agent in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostilled/legalized Power of Attorney authorizing the New Zealand registered agent to file the incorporation application
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or Consul in the jurisdiction where the power of attorney is executed

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML bank reference or PEP clearance letter for each UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Maintaining bank of the UBO or director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization where the bank letter is formally executed; otherwise notarized first-generation copy

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, New Zealand Sanctions Act 2019 designations, and New Zealand Police PEP database. Enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs, family members, and close associates. Continuous sanctions-list monitoring is required, with trigger-based rescreening at onboarding, material ownership change, and at least annually.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Company Register (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz; administered under the Companies Act 1993 and New Zealand Business Number Act 2016)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin-script characters; both English and te reo Māori names are accepted. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin-script phonemes, and an English translation or transliteration must be provided upon request. The name must not be misleading, offensive, or imply Crown, government, or statutory status under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of Companies within 20 working days of the notification of refusal. The request must address each stated ground, provide evidence of distinctiveness, and include any required written consent from the relevant New Zealand government department or statutory body. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, the applicant may apply to the High Court of New Zealand for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016. A fresh name application may also be filed after 20 working days if the rejection risk factors are remedied.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for an e-commerce operation under ISIC 4791 using a New Zealand registered agent, provided there is a physical New Zealand street address where service of process and company records can be maintained. A post-office box alone does not satisfy the registered office requirement under the Companies Act 1993.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 3% estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the Companies Office or an AML/CFT supervisor for a standard low-risk e-commerce company; likelihood increases only upon a suspicion report, complaint, or sanctions/PEP trigger.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), ss.13-18 (incorporation, application and certificate of registration), ss.24-29 (company name), s.34 (pre-registration contracts), ss.42-50 (shares, allotment and shareholder rights), ss.122-124 (registered office and address for service), ss.131-137 (directors duties), ss.152-154 (appointment and removal of directors), ss.200-211 (shareholder remedies), and First Schedule default constitution rules; Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (reporting); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT obligations of payment platforms).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Tarapi Kaporeihana), an operational business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the New Zealand Companies Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online Application for Company Incorporation (electronic statutory application on the Companies Register, including prescribed consents), resulting in a Certificate of Incorporation issued under s.18 of the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. At least one share of any class must be subscribed and allotted to the incorporating shareholder upon registration, and shares may be partly paid or unpaid. No escrow account, capital deposit, capital duty, or notarised capital verification is required under New Zealand law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [INTERNATIONAL COMPANY LIMITED] (NZBN [TBA]). UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTIONS adopted by the sole director and ratified by the shareholder on [DATE], pursuant to ss.122 and 154 of the Companies Act 1993. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED that the subscription for, allotment and issue of 100 ordinary shares of NZ$1.00 each, comprising the issued capital of the Company, be and is hereby approved; the directors are authorised to enter the subscribers in the share register and issue definitive share certificates. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be located at [physical street address, New Zealand], and the Registrar of Companies is hereby notified of the same as the default address for service of documents. 3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED that [full name, date of birth] be and is hereby appointed as sole Director and that [firm/name] be appointed as Company Secretary, each to serve until resignation or removal under the Constitution and the Companies Act 1993. 4. BANKING AND PAYMENT RAILS: RESOLVED that the Director be authorised to open bank accounts and to execute agreements with Stripe and PayPal for the electronic retailing of pet supplies and pet care devices. These resolutions take effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Search and Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online name availability search on the Companies Register; IPONZ (Intellectual Property Office of New Zealand) for trademark conflict screening.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-incorporation name search via the publicly accessible Companies Register to confirm that the proposed name is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing reserved or registered name under s.24 of the Companies Act 1993. Screen the name against the IPONZ trademark register and the .nz domain rules administered by InternetNZ. The name must not imply Crown connection, contain restricted words, or be offensive. Submit up to three alternatives in priority order for use in the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (primary and two alternates)
Signed name consent from any third party whose name appears in the proposed company name (if applicable)
IPONZ trademark search report (recommended)
Domain name availability confirmation (optional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects the name as unavailable or contrary to ss.24-25, the applicant may select an available alternative already filed within the application, or apply under s.25(2) for the Registrar's consent to use a similar name upon provision of written consent from the owner of the existing name or evidence of prior use; re-file the corrected application within 20 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Constitution and Initial Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: External legal counsel or registered chartered accountant; no government filing is made at this stage.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company constitution, or elect to rely on the default constitution set out in the First Schedule of the Companies Act 1993. If a custom constitution is used, it must be signed by each named shareholder before incorporation. Prepare the share allotment schedule and the register of directors' and shareholders' consents, and adopt the financial reporting policy. For the International Company structure, the governance documents should include reserved powers clauses, non-resident director eligibility, a physical address for service in New Zealand, and clauses permitting remote board meetings and electronic execution.
required_dossiers: Company constitution (custom instrument or election to adopt statutory default rules)
Signed consents of shareholders and directors
Share allotment and register draft
Registered office consent from the property owner or landlord
Privacy Act 2020 statement regarding collection of directors' personal details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficiencies in the constitution are curable by amending the instrument prior to filing. Where the online application is returned for correction, the amended constitution and consents may be re-uploaded without losing priority, provided the application is re-submitted within 20 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Application for Company Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Companies Register online portal (https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the Companies Register using a verified RealMe login, select 'Apply to incorporate a company', and complete the statutory declaration of compliance with s.15 of the Companies Act 1993. Enter the company name, address for service and registered office (a physical New Zealand street address, not a P.O. Box), the proposed financial year end, shareholder allocation, and director details including residential address and date of birth. Attach all signed consents and the constitution if customised. Pay the NZ$150 incorporation fee by debit or credit card or from an online credit account and submit. The Registrar examines the application under ss.16-17.
required_dossiers: Completed online incorporation application
Signed consent to act as director (for each director)
Signed consent to act as shareholder (for each shareholder)
Company constitution (if adopting a custom constitution)
Proof of physical registered office address (landlord consent or utility bill)
Passport scan of each director for service-provider AML purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried by the Companies Office, the applicant receives a deficiency notice identifying the defect. The applicant may correct and resubmit through the online dashboard within 20 working days, or file a fresh application; fees are refunded for applications withdrawn before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN Allocation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and New Zealand Business Number Registrar (business.govt.nz).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful examination, the Registrar registers the company under s.17, issues a Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company number, and automatically allocates a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). The company has the capacity, rights, powers and privileges of a natural person from the date of incorporation (s.16 and s.34). Download and securely archive the certificate and the company extract, and verify that the registered office, director and shareholding details appear correctly on the public register.
required_dossiers: Application reference number and online receipt
Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar
NZBN confirmation advice
Company Extract from the Companies Register (for banking and KYC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Bona fide administrative errors on the certificate (such as spelling or dates) may be corrected by filing a 'Rectification of Company Record' request with the Companies Office. Inaccurate director or address information is corrected through an online change-of-particulars form within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Registration and Tax Classification (IRD Number)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, apply for an IRD number. For the International Company engaged in e-commerce, complete the online IRD application (IR596 for non-resident incorporated companies, or the standard online form for a New Zealand-resident company) identifying tax residence based on place of incorporation and central management and control. Use the NZBN to pre-populate company data. Where the company is fully foreign-owned and non-resident managed, notify IRD of the tax-exempt treatment of offshore foreign-sourced income (subject to attribution and separate-account requirements) and register for any required resident withholding tax (RWT) or approved issuer levy (AIL).
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Directors' and shareholders' personal details (IRD numbers if resident, foreign TINs if non-resident)
Projected foreign income statement or initial financial projections
Company constitution and share register
Completed IR596 or online IRD registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD application is queried or delayed, provide amended details through myIR within 20 working days; apply for late-registration relief and seek administrative suspension of penalties and interest under s.144 of the Tax Administration Act 1994.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GST, ACC and Goods Compliance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue; ACC (Accident Compensation Corporation); Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) and New Zealand Customs Service (for imported physical pet goods).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for GST through myIR where annual supplies to New Zealand exceed NZ$60,000, or voluntarily, to recover input GST on third-party warehousing, fulfilment and advertising costs. For remote electronic supplies of pet products to New Zealand consumers, apply the GST-on-remote-services rules and lodge returns electronically. Register with ACC for employer cover if hiring staff, and file a workplace safety statement under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015. For imported physical pet supplies or care devices, lodge a biosecurity clearance and obtain tariff classification with MPI and the New Zealand Customs Service under the Biosecurity Act 1993 and Customs and Excise Act 2018.
required_dossiers: IRD number confirmation
GST registration application (myIR)
ACC employer registration and workplace safety statement (if employees)
Product SKU list and country-of-origin certificates for imported pet goods
NZ Customs tariff classification (HS 3926, 9503 or other applicable heading)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where GST or ACC registration is declined or objected, file a notice of proposed adjustment for GST or apply for an ACC classification review within 60 days. For biosecurity non-compliance, submit a biosecurity clearance or apply for a transitional facility permit under the Biosecurity Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Payment-Rail Onboarding (Stripe and PayPal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed New Zealand banks; Stripe (NZD) and PayPal as reporting entities under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, supervised by the Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) for non-bank payment service providers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a New Zealand business bank account by presenting the certificate of incorporation, company extract, NZBN certificate, IRD number confirmation, and beneficial-ownership declarations. For Stripe, activate an account by providing the NZBN, IRD number, registered office, projected processing volume, product description (ISIC 4791 pet supplies), and settlement bank details, and complete the know-your-business (KYB) verification. For PayPal Business, complete the business verification and link the company bank account. Where the payment platform is itself a reporting entity, establish an ongoing AML/CFT compliance programme, including a compliance officer, if processing volumes exceed applicable thresholds.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN certificate
IRD number letter
Company extract dated within 30 days
Director's passport and residential address proof
Shareholder and beneficial-ownership declarations with source of funds
Projected sales volumes and product descriptions (pet supplies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or payment platform rejects the application, obtain a formal declination letter and resubmit under enhanced due diligence, providing a board resolution, a local agent appointment, and an audited structure chart; alternatively, escalate to the Department of Internal Affairs as the anti-money-laundering supervisor for a procedural review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 4791 (electronic retailing of pet supplies); the New Zealand Companies Office and Inland Revenue are the only mandatory authorities. If warehousing and importation of pet care devices or supplies is conducted, the Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) and New Zealand Customs Service become relevant for biosecurity, tariffs and product-safety border controls.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific operating licence is required for the electronic retailing of pet supplies under New Zealand law; the company operates under its Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN. If physical pet food is manufactured or imported, registration as a Risk Management Programme (RMP) operator under the Animal Products Act 1999, or a pet-food export notice, may become applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand, with territorial authorities acting under the Resource Management Act 1991 (RMA).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category C (No EIA / permitted activity) for fully electronic commerce and light-use office or warehousing without point-source discharge; activity thresholds are not exceeded and no significant adverse effects are present; no mandatory national environmental standard is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater discharge to water or land arises from typical e-retail operations. Where a warehouse or dispatch hub is used, stormwater consents must comply with regional council rules. Refrigerants used in any cold-chain pet-care products must comply with the Ozone Protection and Synthetic Greenhouse Gas Management Act 2006. Plastic packaging and product wrapping must meet Ministry for the Environment packaging recycling thresholds and the Waste Minimisation Act 2008. VOC emissions from aerosolised pet-care preparations must remain below the limits in the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality (2011, as amended).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification: where physical business premises are occupied, a Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) must be current under the Building Act 2004, and an approved fire evacuation scheme must be registered with Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) under s.68 of the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017. Occupational clearance: duties under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 (HSWA) require a written worker health and safety policy, a hazard register, worker engagement, and a permit-to-work system for any warehouse machinery. Structural load adequacy of storage racks must be certified by a chartered professional engineer under the Building Act 2004, and any earthquake-prone building notice must be remediated within statutory time frames.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Taake), Wellington, New Zealand; taxpayer portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must apply to the IRD for a New Zealand IRD number, which is the statutory taxpayer identification number; there is no separate VAT/GST registration number. An eligible International Company applying from outside New Zealand should use Form IR742 (IRD number application for a non-resident company) and provide certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, director/shareholder particulars, a New Zealand contact or registered office, and confirmation of non-residence where relevant. After obtaining an IRD number, the entity registers for GST electronically through myIR using the GST registration process. Foreign companies also registered on the New Zealand Companies Register as an overseas company must provide their NZ Company Number. The same IRD number is used for income tax, GST, and other tax obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not apply a United States-style check-the-box election. Available elections include the election to become a Look-Through Company (LTC) for qualifying New Zealand-resident companies, election for Māori authority tax treatment, and certain GST treatment elections. Hybrid mismatch rules apply under New Zealand tax law to recharacterise or deny deductions for hybrid entities and instruments. For an International Company treated as a non-resident and not deriving New Zealand-source income, no entity classification election is required; if it otherwise carries on business in New Zealand, entity-level income tax applies to New Zealand-source income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — New Zealand VAT-style consumption tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 (annual taxable supplies in the last 12 months or expected next 12 months; the threshold also applies to offshore suppliers of remote services and digital goods supplied to New Zealand consumers; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not operate a real-time tax clearance or continuous transaction control (CTC) regime. GST tax invoices must contain the prescribed particulars, and GST-registered persons must file periodic GST returns through myIR. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates on the Peppol New Zealand network; there is no mandatory government fiscal stamping, digital approval, or per-invoice IRD clearance requirement. Records, including export evidence, must be retained for seven years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST-registered supplier may zero-rate supplies of goods that are physically exported from New Zealand by the supplier within 28 days, including e-commerce sales of pet products to non-resident customers. Zero-rating also applies to certain services supplied to non-residents, including remotely supplied services received outside New Zealand, provided the recipient is outside New Zealand and the supply is not connected with land or goods situated in New Zealand. The supplier must hold contemporaneous documentary evidence proving export, delivery, and payment from the foreign customer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: NZ Customs electronic export declaration (export entry or export manifest)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from New Zealand
Commercial invoice and packing list itemising the PET pet supplies and pet care devices
Inward remittance certificate or New Zealand bank statement proving export proceeds received and FX repatriated within the 180-day window
GST tax invoice for the zero-rated sale and any transport or logistics contracts
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The IRD may audit zero-rated export claims and require proof of physical export, genuine offshore supply, and repatriation of proceeds. If substantiation fails, the supply is reassessed at 15% GST, input credits are clawed back, and use-of-money interest runs from the original return date. Civil shortfall penalties range from 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, and up to 150% for evasion or an abusive tax position. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims are prosecutable under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and may attract criminal fines and imprisonment. Reassessment and clawback may extend to prior periods, and deliberate falsification of export documentation may also trigger Customs offences.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Putea Matua), operating solely as the central bank and monetary authority; foreign exchange policy is liberalized and administered by the Bank under the non-statutory framework of New Zealand's no-exchange-control regime, with the Overseas Investment Office (OIO) exercising prudential oversight only for 'sensitive' asset acquisitions and the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) supervising FX derivative providers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains full and free convertibility on both current and capital account. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is a free-floating, freely tradeable currency with no quantitative exchange controls, no central bank permission requirements for inbound or outbound payments, and no obstacles to the repatriation of profits, dividends, royalties, interest, or liquidation proceeds. Since the abolition of exchange controls in 1984, neither the Reserve Bank of New Zealand nor the Treasury imposes approval gates or surrender quotas. The only compliance frictions are generic: AML/CFT reporting under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (including prescribed transaction reports for cash over NZD 10,000), and the potential application of Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) or Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) on outbound interest and dividend flows, which are assessable under tax law rather than FX regulation. The subject International Company, classified as Tax_Exempt_Zone, will enjoy unrestricted capital mobility through the standard banking system, provided its beneficial ownership documentation and source-of-funds evidence satisfy bank due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no mandatory surrender, no forced repatriation timing, and no statutory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds in NZD or any foreign currency may be retained indefinitely in offshore accounts or held in New Zealand foreign-currency bank accounts. There are no Reserve Bank directions requiring settlement within a specific number of days and no percentage-based conversion obligations. The only applicable obligation is evidentiary: export documentation (commercial invoices, packing lists, customs declarations) must be retained for AML/CFT and tax audit purposes, and any transaction involving physical cash movement above NZD 10,000 must be reported to the New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit. For the subject e-commerce retail operation, payment settlement from Stripe and PayPal into NZD or USD accounts is unrestricted and fully retainable.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (NZD current account with internet banking, SWIFT and PayTo/Autopay facilities)
Operational Account (NZD business transaction account with online banking and FastNet Classic treasury portal)
Operational Account (NZD Business Complete account with NetBank, e-invoicing, and trade finance desk)
Operational Account with Multi-Currency (NZD + USD + AUD) facility and integrated FX hedging line
Capital Escrow / Foreign-Currency Clearing Account (NZD and USD, with Global Wallet connectivity to HSBC Group entities)
Operational Account (NZD retail-business account, suitable for low-volume local settlements; limited cross-border trade finance depth)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH for non-resident-owned e-commerce entities. New Zealand-licensed financial technology providers and Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) that hold a Financial Service Provider (FSP) registration and are supervised by the FMA, or are registered as money remitters under the AML/CFT Act 2009, are legally viable. Providers such as Airwallex (NZ FSP), Wise New Zealand, and Payoneer can issue multi-currency settlement accounts with virtual IBANs/NZ bank account numbers, enabling seamless Stripe/PayPal sweeps. Legal constraints: (i) the EMI must maintain a local anti-money laundering compliance officer; (ii) the International Company must pass beneficial-ownership disclosure equivalent to Tier-1 bank standards; (iii) EMI accounts typically do not provide credit facilities, letters of credit, or interest-bearing treasury products; (iv) some EMIs decline jurisdictions with offshore trust structures unless the trust deed and source of wealth are exhaustively documented. For the subject low-risk e-commerce profile, a hybrid structure of an NZ Tier-1 parent operational account plus a global EMI (e.g., Airwallex) for cross-border supplier disbursement is the most efficient configuration.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand banks do not impose a uniform statutory mandate requiring in-person board appearances. In practice, Tier-1 banks offer remote onboarding for low-risk companies, including video-verified identification of directors and beneficial owners via a chartered accountant or registered lawyer's certification. However, at least one director or authorised signatory who is a natural person will be required to complete a live video call with the bank's compliance team; a physical visit to a branch in Auckland, Wellington, or Christchurch is typically triggered only if the company's beneficial ownership is held through an offshore trust or opaque jurisdiction. For the subject CK_IC International Company, remote opening is highly probable if: (i) the New Zealand registered agent is appointed; (ii) directors hold passports from FATF-listed jurisdictions; and (iii) the board supply a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation and any tax-exempt status confirmation. A physical presence waiver may be granted for companies whose principal transactions are settled via regulated payment processors (Stripe/PayPal).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership held through an offshore trust or International Company (Cook Islands-style) creating opacity in the ultimate controller chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory Declaration as to Beneficial Ownership executed by the trust's registered trustee; certified copy of the full trust deed and any variation of trust; a corporate chart mapping every intermediate company to individual ultimate beneficial owners; notarized passport and proof of residential address for each UBO; and an independent legal opinion from a New Zealand-qualified solicitor confirming the true control chain and the absence of any nominee arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity, low-value card-not-present transactions in an e-commerce environment with no physical storefront
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month settlement statements from Stripe and PayPal showing transaction history and net volumes; a copy of the merchant agreement with Stripe/PayPal; the live storefront URL and proof of domain ownership; product catalog screenshots; customer refund and chargeback policy documentation; ISS/PCI-DSS compliance attestation; and a current complaint log demonstrating adequate consumer protection practices in compliance with the Fair Trading Act 1986 and Privacy Act 2020.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected cross-border outbound payment flows to Asian pet-product suppliers without an established trade history in New Zealand
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial invoices and Master Supply Agreement for each principal supplier; customs import declarations and Ministry for Primary Industries biosecurity clearance records for pet products; a projected 12-month cash-flow budget showing match between payment currency and revenue currency; proof that supplier bank accounts are held in jurisdictions with functional AML regimes; and a letter from the supplier confirming the commercial relationship and the purpose of each disbursement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No physical company office or substantive operations in New Zealand beyond a registered agent, raising residence and economic-substance doubts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A lease agreement or co-working membership for a physical (even serviced) office; payroll records for a local part-time administrator; New Zealand Inland Revenue (IRD) number confirmation and Goods and Services Tax registration (if applicable); utility bills or postal-service contracts in the company's name; a board resolution confirming the decision to maintain minimal physical presence consistent with e-commerce substance; and evidence of New Zealand supervision of the company's records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors resident in multiple tax jurisdictions causing mismatch in tax identification and CRS/FATCA self-certification inconsistencies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OECD Common Reporting Standard (CRS) self-certification forms (Form NZ for New Zealand, and equivalent W-8/W-9) completed consistently for each director and UBO; documentary evidence of tax residency in each jurisdiction; an auditor-confirmed register of significant shareholders; and a prior-year corporate income tax return or tax-exempt clearances from the relevant revenue authority, plus completed Internal Revenue Service (IRS) FATCA classification forms where U.S. persons are involved.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital subscription from the offshore parent or shareholder must be executed via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank cover) into the New Zealand operational account held at a Tier-1 bank. Compliant protocol: (i) obtain a board resolution authorizing the capital contribution and specifying whether it is equity injection or subordinated shareholder loan; (ii) if equity, make entries in the company's share register and, for NZ company law purposes, advise Companies Office of any issue of shares to non-resident persons; (iii) the remitting bank must use a purpose code or payment description explicitly stating 'Share Capital Subscription' or 'Capital Injection - ISIC 4791 E-Commerce'; (iv) the receiving bank will credit the NZD account in real-time via the ESAS settlement system; (v) if the amount exceeds NZD 50,000, the receiving bank will request supporting evidence including the board resolution, source-of-funds statement, and UBO identification; (vi) no OIO consent is required because an e-commerce retail business does not constitute 'sensitive land', 'significant business assets', or fishing quota, unless the relevant 25% or more ownership threshold is crossed by a non-resident; (vii) for amounts in USD or AUD, the bank may auto-convert at the prevailing interbank rate or route through the multi-currency account, subject to the exchange rate and the bank's market-marker spread. A receipt confirmation (MT910) should be reconciled against the company's internal cash ledger.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements are: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments where the beneficiary is known and the amount is below LC thresholds, with the reference field containing the invoice number and purchase order ID to satisfy audit trail; (2) Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) issued via SWIFT MT700 for high-value or first-time supplier relationships, with payment upon presentation of compliant shipping documents; (3) Documentary Collections (MT400/MT422) for trusted Asian suppliers seeking lower costs than LC; (4) for payment processor disbursements, Stripe and PayPal settlement in NZD will be initiated by the processors via SWIFT or via their local New Zealand clearing arrangements (BECS/ESAS) into the designated bank account, with a settlement delay of typically 2-7 banking days; (5) intra-NZD government and tax payments, if any, will clear via BECS and Inland Revenue's payment channels; and (6) supplier payments to New Zealand domestic vendors will use the Bulk Electronic Clearing System (BECS) / PayTo rail. For FX conversion associated with outbound disbursements, the bank's treasury desk executes at the NZD spot rate; no surrender or conversion approval is required. Any payment to a jurisdiction under an OFAC/UN sanctions embargo will trigger an automated block and compliance referral, so the supplier master list must be screened against the NZ Sanctions Register and OFAC SDN list.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after the company's annual incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the annual return is not delivered by the statutory date, the Registrar issues a default notice and may strike the company off the New Zealand Register after 20 working days' notice; directors and the company remain liable for penalties and costs of prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Statements for large or Financial Markets Conduct (FMC) reporting entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not later than six months after the balance date of the annual accounting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-lodgement exposes the company and directors to enforcement action by the Financial Markets Authority, civil penalties, and director prosecution; the Registrar may also initiate removal proceedings for persistent non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies if the company is a large company (total assets exceeding NZ$3 million or total revenue exceeding NZ$3 million in the relevant two preceding accounting periods), is an FMC reporting entity, or is validly requisitioned by shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares. Small companies below these thresholds are generally exempt from compulsory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP), comprising New Zealand equivalents to IFRS for Tier 1; NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime for Tier 2; and NZ IFRS for Small and Medium-sized Entities for eligible small companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual return serves as the annual UBO confirmation. It must certify the current directors, members, and significant controllers as at the anniversary date, and any share transfer during the preceding year must be reflected in the register of members and the annual return. The company must maintain its Register of Significant Controllers and notify the Registrar of any significant-control change within 10 business days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of directors' and shareholder meetings
